page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro System and custom 64-bit ARM-based Graviton2 processors (ARMv8 Neoverse-N1). The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs with 1 thread per physical core clocked at 2.5 GHz, supported by 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. It is paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes a baseline network bandwidth allocation of 6 Gbps without hardware GPU acceleration.

A central feature of the im4gn.xlarge is its bundled local storage, offering 1875 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD capacity. Benchmark evaluations highlight solid storage and data manipulation capabilities, posting an average ranking in PassMark database operations and moderate uncached memory bandwidth throughput (69.63 GB/sec read and 33.78 GB/sec write). Stress-ng metrics demonstrate average baseline performance for both single-core (1519.89) and multi-core (6054.65) synthetic CPU load.

The Neoverse-N1 cores exhibit trade-offs in raw compute-heavy and vector tasks, scoring in lower percentiles for Geekbench single-core (936.0), Geekbench multi-core (3191.0), and PassMark encryption tests. Similarly, compression workloads and LLM inference speeds reflect entry-level compute capacity. From an architectural efficiency perspective, the dedicated ARM core mapping eliminates hyper-threading contention and provides consistent execution, while integrated local NVMe reduces secondary cloud storage overheads.

The hardware configuration of the im4gn.xlarge makes it appropriate for distributed NoSQL databases, search indexes, log analytics agents, caching layers, and intermediate ETL staging where high-speed local disk capacity is required alongside moderate memory and CPU demands.
description: Amazon Web Services im4gn.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and ARM64-based Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 architecture. Equipped with 4 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz, 16.0 GB of memory, and 6 Gbps baseline networking, its key hardware component is 1875 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results place its database processing and stress-ng CPU execution in the middle performance tier, alongside steady uncached memory read bandwidth of 69.63 GB/sec. Conversely, intensive instruction sets, decompression, and machine learning inference exhibit lower relative scores due to modest per-core throughput. Delivering high-capacity local disk density alongside non-hyperthreaded ARM cores, the im4gn.xlarge serves workloads such as transactional data stores, search indexing nodes, log ingestion pipelines, and local caching servers.
